title: Microdeploy stitchboard and annotated release draft — Jun 2026 (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playpad for a constrained microdeploy (limited user cohort, region-first) to ship small critical runtime tweaks and an observability change. Goal is low blast radius with fast rollback if any latency/accuracy regressions appear.

Scope for this microdeploy:
- Runtime kernel change: reduce attention-window prefetch on 1s/2s batch flows (opt-level: kPrefetch=2)
- Telemetry: emit per-route token-latency percentile tags and a short-lived tag to identify cohort users
- Console: add lightweight per-route quota throttling toggle (feature flag only, no enforcement on first roll)

High-level roll plan (compact calendar):
- Fri 2026-06-18 07:00-09:00 UTC: Dry run in staging (smoke + perf harness) — owners: Evan, Marco
- Mon 2026-06-21 02:00-06:00 UTC: Canary rollout to 0.5% global traffic (region us-west-2 prioritized) — owners: Aisha, Priya
- Mon 2026-06-21 06:00-12:00 UTC: Observability window, telemetry sampling ramp to 100% for cohort calls — owners: Observability on-call
- Tue 2026-06-22 02:00-10:00 UTC: Gradual increase to 5% if KPIs stable (latency p95 < baseline + 5%, error rate delta < 0.1%)
- Wed 2026-06-23 02:00-08:00 UTC: Decision point to continue full rollout or roll back — owners: Release owner and SRE

Preflight checklist (must be green before canary):
- [ ] Staging run results uploaded to /s3/release/microdeploy-2026-06/staging-summary.json (Evan)
- [ ] Perf harness baseline captured (last 7 days median) and compared (Marco)
- [ ] Smoke tests: generation fidelity sanity, kv-cache integrity, API contract conformance (Priya)
- [ ] Canary config prepared in k8s-configs/canary/microdeploy-0618.yaml (Aisha)
- [ ] Rollback artifact (previous image/tag) staged and smoke-verified (Aisha)
- [ ] Pager rotation confirmed for rollout window and midnight fallback (SRE lead)
- [ ] Slack #release-watch channel pinned with runbook and on-call list (Priya)

Smoke test matrix (quick reference):
- API contract: v1/generate, v1/chat, v1/embeddings -> sanity checks pass
- KV-cache: cold start & warm queries -> kv-cache hits within expected window
- Latency: single-token generation under 250ms p50 in canary subject (baseline depends on model)
- Chaos: small packet loss injected in staging run (5%) -> no timeouts above baseline+10%

KPI guardrails (automated checks):
- Latency p95 delta must be < +5% vs baseline for 30m rolling window
- Error rate delta must be < +0.1% absolute vs baseline for 30m window
- Token cost trend must not spike > +8% over baseline (alert if triggered)
- If any threshold trips, automated safety lane reduces canary traffic to 0% (rollback) and notifies #release-watch

Rollback plan (fastest path):
1) Trigger rollback via release-service: set image tag to previous (tag: runtime-2026-06-08) and set canary weight 0%
2) Run post-rollback smoke (3 quick requests per route) and verify latency and error metrics returned to baseline
3) Open postmortem stub and assign blameless owner (release owner)
4) If rollback fails, escalate to infra-sre with runbook reference (page list is in the channel)

Communication templates (short form):
- Slack #release-watch (to channel):
  "Starting canary rollout for microdeploy-2026-06 at 02:00 UTC (0.5% traffic, us-west-2). Watch KPIs: latency p95, error-rate, token-cost. If you see anomalies, tag @sre-oncall and @aisha.patel."
- Email to stakeholders (30m after canary start):
  Subject: Microdeploy-2026-06 Canary update — 30m
  Body: Canary at 0.5% (us-west-2). Latency p95 delta: +0.8%. Error rate delta: +0.02%. No rollout action required at this time. Next check at +2h.

Draft release notes (to be trimmed for PROD release page):
- Summary: Small runtime optimization to attention prefetch and added per-route latency tagging to improve performance visibility. This microdeploy targets low-risk cohorts for initial verification.
- Features:
  - Reduced attention prefetch for short-burst workloads (opt-level: kPrefetch=2) which aims to reduce GPU memory churn on medium-length sequences.
  - Per-route token-latency p50/p95 tagging surfaced to telemetry for faster triage.
  - Feature-flagged throttling toggle added to console (no enforcement in this pilot).
- Bug fixes:
  - Fix: kv-cache eviction edge case where a stale entry could cause small latency spikes (internal only).
- Known issues:
  - Minor metric-schema drift observed in staging for a subset of embeddings routes; instrumentation change pending (tracked in ENG-4678).

Telemetry dashboard quick links (to be created):
- microdeploy/latency-p95-by-route (rollout cohort filter)
- microdeploy/error-rate-signal (30m, 1h)
- microdeploy/token-cost-delta (rolling 6h)

Post-release tasks (first 48h):
- [ ] 2h, 6h, 12h checks posted to #release-watch with short summary (owners: Priya/Evan)
- [ ] Evaluate telemetry retention delta (Marco)
- [ ] Collate any user-facing anomalies and prepare patch plan if needed
- [ ] Move feature flag from "pilot" to "monitor" or revert by EOD+1 if unstable

Notes to self / open questions (WIP):
- We need a small synthetic workload to specifically target the attention-prefetch code path; current perf harness focuses on longer sequences. Marco to prototype by 6/16.
- Should we enable enforcement for throttling toggle in a later microdeploy or leave as pure telemetry for 2 weeks? (Pro: quicker safety experiments. Con: risk of unexpected throttling behavior)
- Risk: upstream model changes (new quantized checkpoints) scheduled next week — coordinate windows to avoid concurrent canaries. Added calendar invite to block 6/21-6/23.

Appendix: quick commands
- Set canary weight: curl -XPOST https://release-service.internal/set-weight -d '{"service":"runtime","tag":"microdeploy-2026-06","weight":0.005}'
- Trigger rollback: ./bin/release rollback runtime microdeploy-2026-06 --to-tag=runtime-2026-06-08

-- end working draft --
